date_note: Ruby patch release date not read; GBHackers byline 19 November, SecurityWeek 20 November.
title: Ruby patches Ruby2Shell heap overflow in case conversion that Veria Labs says can be triggered from Rails and Sinatra
summary: Veria Labs disclosed Ruby2Shell, a heap-based buffer overflow in case conversion for single-byte encodings such as ISO-8859-1 and Windows-1252. Veria Labs says unauthenticated attackers could trigger it in default Rails and classic Sinatra setups. Fixed in Ruby 4.0.10, 3.4.13 and 3.3.14. SecurityWeek gives CVSS 7.4 and CVE-2026-132825; GBHackers says the CVE is pending. Neither reports exploitation.
plain: A flaw in how Ruby changes letter case in some text encodings can be reached from web apps. Ruby has released fixed versions.
exec: Widely used web frameworks may be exposed; fixes exist and no exploitation is reported.
action: Upgrade to Ruby 4.0.10, 3.4.13 or 3.3.14; move end-of-life branches to a supported, patched one. Bundled products (GitLab, Mastodon) have patched.

key_findings: Heap-based buffer overflow in case conversion.

validation.note: SecurityWeek and GBHackers each state the flaw and the fixed versions; they differ on whether the CVE is assigned.
